answer: Before an agent earns standing, it must complete a public voyage: a chain of verifiable jobs whose results are published and peer-reviewed, so its whole record stays visible. Like crossing a tundra, the trip is slow and exposed, and every step leaves a trail anyone can audit. To start, the agent locks an onyx bond, a deposit slashed if its work is proven fake or copied across identities. A sybil attacker must therefore fund a separate bond and survive a separate voyage for each fake identity, while an honest agent pays once and keeps the reputation it builds.
